subject: Post-call compliance action log: BAA availability & deployment options

Subject: Post-call compliance action log: BAA availability & deployment options

Hi Emily / Samir — thanks again for a productive call earlier. Quick recap and action items (TL;DR at the top):

TL;DR
- MediWell expects PHI ingestion for the POC (patient notes) — BAA required.
- MediWell leaning toward Dedicated capacity for initial POC; wants details on timelines and KMS options.
- Redwood can provide SOC 2 Type II evidence (attached) and a draft BAA for review (attached).

Notes from the call:
- Scope: ingestion of anonymized + identified patient notes via API, initial volume ~5k requests/day for POC.
- PHI boundary question: MediWell asked whether Redwood stores derived metadata or raw text beyond inference windows — short answer below from Aditya.

Action items / next steps (owners in parentheses):
1) I will send the SOC 2 summary and our standard BAA draft for legal review (Lauren) — attached: SOC2-summary-20271115.pdf, draft_BAA_template_MediWell.docx.
2) Aditya to confirm technical PHI boundaries, KMS options, and recommended deployment modes for PHI workloads (Aditya).
3) Neha to initiate security questionnaire intake and share the hosted link for MediWell to complete (Neha).
4) Schedule a technical deep-dive next week to finalize POC architecture and timelines (Lauren) — propose 30-min slot: https://cal.redwood.com/lauren/30min.

Notes on immediate asks for MediWell team: please confirm the following so we can tailor the POC:
- Intended deployment mode for POC: Hosted (with BAA), Dedicated (reserved GPU pool), or Private (VPC / on-prem).
- Primary data flow: will PHI be sent to the API in identifiable form, or will you pseudonymize before sending?
- Required compliance evidence beyond SOC 2 (e.g., HITRUST) and any internal questionnaire items to prioritize.

Attachments: SOC2-summary-20271115.pdf (summary + control mapping), draft_BAA_template_MediWell.docx, redwood-map-poc-milestones.xlsx (milestone list).

Thanks — I’ll coordinate with Aditya and Neha and follow up with proposed times for the technical deep-dive.

Best,

Thanks Lauren — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side and follow-up questions: 

- Confirmed: MediWell will send identifiable patient notes for the POC (we will not pseudonymize initially; that is a later step). That means we need a signed BAA before any PHI is processed.
- Deployment preference: we are leaning toward Dedicated for the POC to keep latency predictable and ensure isolation. If Dedicated is straightforward to stand up, that’s our preference.
- SOC 2: quick question — is the SOC 2 Type II report date in 2027 or 2026? We need the most recent opinion for our security team.
- KMS / encryption: can you confirm whether Dedicated supports customer-managed keys (we have an AWS KMS requirement)?
- Security questionnaire: please send the intake link / Doc for our security team — we’ll route it to them this week.

We also have two compliance-specific asks from our legal/security reviewers:
1) High-level dataflow diagram for PHI during inference and any ephemeral caches (they want to confirm no persistent storage of raw PHI).
2) SLA expectations around deletion requests and retention — e.g., upon contract termination or data purge requests.

Happy to schedule the technical deep-dive — Samir is the engineering lead and will join. Available windows: Tue 30th (10–12 PST) or Wed 31st (14–17 PST).

Thanks,
Emily

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Post-call compliance action log: BAA availability & deployment options

Emily — quick technical answers below, summarized first then details. Happy to cover in the deep-dive.

Summary:
- SOC 2 Type II: report opinion date 2027-11-15. Summary attached and full report available via secure share (link below).
- Preferred PHI deployments: Dedicated (recommended) or Private (VPC/on-prem). We will not recommend Hosted for ongoing PHI production unless you require it and accept additional controls/limits.
- KMS: Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS) for disk and key material; Private supports your KMS/HSM. Hosted can be configured with BYOK in some enterprise arrangements, but not by default for self-serve.
- PHI boundary: Redwood’s inference runtime processes text in-memory; we do not persist raw payloads to long-term storage by default. We do have transient caches (KV cache) to speed repeated prompts — these can be configured to be disabled for PHI workloads or encrypted at rest with your keys.
- Deletion & retention: we support contractual retention settings and can enforce immediate purge of transient caches and logs for Dedicated/Private; for Hosted we need explicit contract language to guarantee immediate purge behavior.

Technical details / links:
- SOC 2: opinion date 2027-11-15. Full report available to signed partners; summary attached: SOC2-summary-20271115.pdf. Secure access link: https://drive.redwood.com/sr/SOC2-20271115 (will grant after intake).
- BAA: attached draft_BAA_template_MediWell.docx — legal teams often redline Section 3 (Subprocessors) and Section 7 (Data retention).
- KMS & encryption: Dedicated: supports AWS KMS CMKs mapped to instance-level disk encryption and optional runtime key wrapping. Private: support for customer-provided HSM/KMS. Hosted: Redwood-managed keys by default; BYOK possible via enterprise onboarding.
- KV cache behavior: cache lives in encrypted RAM and optionally on local encrypted disk for performance. For PHI POC, we recommend disabling persistent KV cache and enabling per-request ephemeral mode.

Proposed POC configuration (recommended):
- Environment: Dedicated GPU pool in us-west-2 with customer-managed AWS KMS.
- Inference flow: API -> dedicated pool (no persistent storage of raw payloads) -> ephemeral KV cache (disabled/purgeable) -> response returned.
- Compliance artifacts provided: SOC 2 summary, BAA, API audit logs for retention windows, per-request trace IDs for correlation.

I’ll join the technical deep-dive and can prepare a short diagram for the PHI dataflow and an itemized list of configuration knobs (KMS, cache, retention, logging).

Regards,
Aditya Rao
